_comment: E rounds that owe state/nuc-reachability-log.jsonl a row and provably cannot pay. Read by reachability_check.load_declared_holes / log_coverage (round 454). An entry is an assertion that a round has LOOKED for the evidence and found none -- not that nobody has looked. The bar is high on purpose: round 454 found eight holes and recovered SEVEN of them (190, 220, 226, 250, 280, 292, 442) from logs/round-<N>.json, a source that had been on disk the whole time, so 'no row exists' is nowhere near evidence that no observation survives. log_coverage reports a declared entry that is no longer missing under `declared_but_not_missing` and --strict fails on it: an acknowledgement that suppresses nothing reads as coverage, so if someone recovers a round listed here, DELETE its entry in the same commit.
_why_round_148_is_not_listed: Round 148 was the eighth hole and the only unrecoverable one -- no logs/round-148.json, no state/research-state.md or -archive.md heading, no knowledge/round-148-*.md, and logs/driver.log's own first line is round 152, so nothing records that the round ran at all beyond state/round_counter having passed through it. It is NOT an entry here because log_coverage's population is the driver log, so round 148 is not in the population and there is nothing for a declaration to suppress. Listing it would have made --strict exit 1 forever on a round the check cannot see -- which is precisely the dead-acknowledgement failure the `declared_but_not_missing` field exists to catch, and it caught this one when round 454 tried it. Round 454.
